newsitem.title: USA: GMAC, Integon in merger pact.
newsitem.headline: GMAC, Integon in merger pact.

text.p: General Motors Acceptance Corp and Integon said Monday they had signed a definitive agreement for Integon to merge with a GMAC subsidiary.

The pact gives Integon common stock holders $26 cash per share, including the holders of common stock to be issued upon conversion of Integon's $3.875 convertible preferred stock, or an aggregate of about $550 million.
Integon shares were halted Monday with a last trade of $16 a share.
General Motors shares closed down 1/8 at 55-1/2.
The companies issued a joint statement Monday evening saying the deal had been unanimously approved by Integon's board. It remains subject to approval by Integon's shareholders.
Integon, based in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, offers nonstandard automobile insurance to consumers who do not qualify for standard rates.
The company reported $800 million in net premiums written in 1996.

"The proposed merger with Integon results from seeking attractive growth alternatives and represents a major step in our efforts to expand our reach in the financial services industry," GMAC President John Rines said in the statement.

Convertible preferred stock of Integon not converted before the effective date of the merger will be redeemed on or after September 16, for $52.33,or the equivalent of about $20 per share of common stock, the companies said.
